newsitem.title: UK: Billiton says UK FID problem resolved.
newsitem.headline: Billiton says UK FID problem resolved.

text.p: South African mining house Billiton, which plans to become a British-listed company later this month, said on Monday that it had resolved problems with the British government over the payment of foreign income dividends (FIDs).
Chief finance officer Mick Davis told reporters the company had been "assured the problems will be resolved."
Last week British finance Minster Gordon Brown included plans to abolish FIDs from 1999 in his budget.
FIDs allow companies to avoid paying tax in Britain on earnings already taxed abroad that are then distributed as dividends.
Abolition would be a particular problem for Billiton, which will make nearly all its profits outside the UK.
Analysts said abolition could lead to a sharp rise in Billiton's tax bill.
